findings.text: BlockDef.untrusted_fields means different things in two units. add-taint-static Decision 2 reads an entry as a path and taints its first segment (`notes.body` gives `notes`; its catalogue C uses `crm.update@1` with `["notes.body"]`). add-block-registry Decision 4 step 6 requires every entry to be an own key of `output.properties` and refuses `notes.body` with `unknown_field`. No shipped block uses a dotted entry, so nothing breaks today, but a block with a nested untrusted field could never be imported.

add-web-flow-graph's parity test requires `GRAPH_NODE_KINDS` to deep-equal U22's `NODE_KINDS` (order included). add-flow-format-model never states the order of `NODE_KINDS`; it only lists the kinds in the `NodeKind` union and the doc-terms scenario. Stating that `NODE_KINDS` follows the union order would settle it.

add-flow-format-model defines `successorFields` only as 'the seed's graph.ts pair' and its scenario covers some kinds. add-web-flow-graph writes out a full table (which kinds have `next`; `cases` read by entries for `human.approval`) and its parity test feeds every kind a node with all fields and odd `cases` keys. The behaviour both units share is not fixed in U22's own spec, for example whether `human.approval` reads `cases` by entries or by the fixed keys approved/rejected/timeout.

add-web-flow-editor's panel registry refuses the ids "Bad Id" and "" and a 61-character title, but states no pattern for a valid id. add-web-flow-graph relies on the id "graph" and the title "Graph" being accepted; its design calls this 'a requirement on U28', but U28's spec does not state it.

This is justified because `src/` cannot import `test/`, but the two loaders can drift apart.

`unresolvedReferences` and `canReach` in add-test-catalogue overlap the validator's L2 registry lookups and its local graph.ts reachability. Both are scoped as a test-only data check, which is acceptable.

findings.text: `loadRegistryCatalogue` is declared `Promise<Catalogue>`, and design Decision 8 says it is "in fact a `RegistryCatalogue`". Yet the scenario "A load reads one tenant and stays fixed" calls `roleNames()` on tenant C's loaded catalogue, which is not a member of `Catalogue`. The test then needs a cast or a narrowing step that nothing specifies. Declaring `Promise<RegistryCatalogue>`, or saying how the test narrows the type, would remove the guess.

In design Decision 11 and § Failure cases, a null `deps.pool` gives 503 `AUTHZ_UNAVAILABLE` on `GET /api/v1/blocks`. No scenario in "Refusals of the list" exercises it. Its relation to the route's `errors` list (`CURSOR_INVALID`, `ENGINE_KEY_REQUIRED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`) and to `unregisteredRouteErrors` is also not stated.

An invalid actor is only caught by `appendAudit` (Decision 5). An import whose entries are all `unchanged`, or an empty one, therefore resolves even when the actor is invalid; the spec does not say whether that is intended. Separately, the scenario "I and the actor `{ kind: "user", id: "" }`" expects `AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID`, which holds only if tenant A does not already hold I. `import.test.ts` combines four scenarios, and tasks.md does not say whether each one gets a fresh database or tenant.

scenario-data.md says tenant C (`tenant_c`) "is inserted with the owner pool". It does not give the insert (the columns of `ursitoare.tenant`) or the `reviewProfile` of the `TenantContext` that `createTestSession(db, c, "cara", clock)` and `loadRegistryCatalogue(db.appPool, c)` need. The order of `blockRefs()` is not fixed: insertion order or sorted by code unit. The only scenario passes I and then M, which is already sorted, so it cannot tell the two apart. Decision 4(4) also leaves open whether the 262144-character limit applies to the raw block minus `binding` or to the normalised definition. For the given scenarios both readings give the same result.

findings.text: Decision 1 puts only `doc.toJS({ maxAliasCount })` inside try/catch and maps a `RangeError` to `FORMAT_TOO_DEEP` there. The scenario with 100000 nested YAML flow brackets (about 200 KB, under `maxBytes`) could exhaust the stack inside `YAML.parseDocument` itself, before `toJS` is called. design.md § Test plan says each test file's inline sample is "a block, an `llm.extract`, a `switch`, an `end`". The parse scenario uses a four-node sample with three `output_schema` fields (one anchor, two aliases), which that list of nodes cannot hold. So the sample list is a description, not a constraint. An implementer can work around this, but the wording conflicts.

The types make `next` optional on `BlockNode`, `HumanFormNode` and `DelegateNode`, and `on_timeout` optional on `DelegateNode`. Yet `requiredSuccessorFields` returns `["next"]` for `block` and `["next", "on_timeout"]` for `human.form` and `delegate`. design.md also says the document types describe a document that has already passed U25's schema layer. Either the types or the meaning of "required" should be stated so the two agree.

The test checks only `max_retries`, so the term list, and therefore what `docs/authoring/format.md` must contain, is left to the implementer's reading.

findings.text: The spec says both create routes take an `Idempotency-Key`, but never says whether the header is required. The save scenarios name a key only for `T2` (`s1`). The `T1` repeat saves, the JSON twin and the "Who may call" saves name no key, which suggests the header is optional. Since `IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER_SCHEMA` is merged, the implementer will probably follow add-admin-api's rule, but this unit should state it.

The audit events are only partly fixed. `flow.version_saved` has a target, an actor and a payload. `flow.created` has a target and a payload but no actor. `flow.version_validated` has only a payload: its target (presumably `{ kind: "flow_version", id: <hash> }`) and its actor are not stated. Later readers of the audit chain depend on these.

Decision 3 lists the U+0000 check after parsing and the name check, and the scenario expects `{ reason: "parse", code: "FORMAT_NOT_JSON" }` for `"# \u0000\n" + T1`. This relies on yaml 2.9.1 accepting a NUL inside a comment. If the parser refuses it, the parse step answers `FORMAT_YAML_SYNTAX` first. The check order (before or after `parseFlowText`) should be fixed so the expected code holds either way. The spec also does not say whether `message` is present in those details.

Several failure paths are not specified. Bad `limit` or `after` arguments to `listFlows` and `listVersions` at the function level have no stated outcome (presumably `FLOW_INVALID`). Two concurrent `createFlow` calls with the same name have no stated outcome (presumably one `FLOW_EXISTS`). The spec does not say how `FLOW_UNKNOWN_TEAM` is told apart from other foreign-key failures, such as an unknown `created_by`.

Design Decision 7 gives full policy ids (`registry-flows-author-edit-own-team`, `registry-flows-team-read`, `registry-flows-list`). It does not say whether the `.cedar` file writes these ids in full or whether the loader adds the `registry-flows-` prefix. No scenario asserts the ids. `ListFilter`, `CursorBinding`, `readPage` and `encodeCursor` are used by name only, with no shapes in `delivered-shapes.md`. They are in the merged code, so the implementer can read them there.

`seedFlowActors` must run `provisionTenantIdp` "once per tenant and database", but the helper is not told how it knows whether that has already run (tracking, or catching a duplicate error) when it is called more than once.

findings.text: Decision 4 resolves `nodes.n.output.p...` (and `hook.output.*`) to `fields[p]` when `p` is an own key, and to `output` otherwise. It never says what a reference to the whole output with an empty path (`nodes.n.output`, `hook.output`) carries. The taken `Ref` type allows `path: []` for `root: "node"`, and the shown part of the format spec neither forbids nor tests `nodes.a.output` with no path. Followed as written, `${{ nodes.fetch_invoice.output }}` would carry `[]`, because RF-1's `fetch_invoice` has `output` `[]` while its `raw_text` and `vendor_name` fields are `untrusted`. That would let data pass through as trusted in a fail-closed security algebra. The spec needs a rule for this case (for example, join `output` with every `fields` entry), plus a scenario that tests it.

Decision 6 requires both functions to be total for any plain-JSON document and to fail closed. But no rule covers malformed hook structures: `flow.hooks` that is not an array (Decision 7 takes `flow.hooks.length`, so a string would count characters), a rule that is not an object, a `match` that is missing or not an object, a selector field that is not a list, a node `pre`/`post` that is not an array, a hook entry that is not an object, or a hook `kind` that is neither `code` nor `block`. These choices change taint (does a malformed rule match every node? Does an unknown hook kind count as a code hook that widens output?) and they change capability sites. No scenario covers any of them, so an implementer could pick a fail-open reading and every test would still pass.

design.md § Interfaces says `from` is "the producing node (for `nodes.*` and `hook.output.*`)". The scenario "Unknown and malformed input fails closed" expects `from: null` for `nodes.ghost.output.x`. The rule should say that a missing node gives `from: null`.

Decision 7 checks the limits "before any work", but the edge count includes "every applying hook, once per wrapped node". Deciding which hooks apply under `effect` selectors needs catalogue lookups, so catalogue calls (and catalogue exceptions) can happen before the edge-limit check. The order of catalogue calls against the limit checks is not fixed.

findings.text: Design decision 12 and the journey scenario need `positions.ts` (which imports `yamlLanguage` from `@codemirror/lang-yaml`) to be imported by `test/` files. The root typecheck runs those files without DOM types (delivered-shapes Facts: root `lib` is `["es2024"]` and `web` is excluded). `@codemirror/lang-yaml` pulls in `@codemirror/language` and `@codemirror/view`, whose declarations refer to DOM types such as `HTMLElement`. The spec does not say whether the root config sets `skipLibCheck`, or what the implementer should do if the root typecheck fails on those declarations. That means `test/journeys/m3-flow-editor.test.ts` and `test/web-flow-editor/*.test.ts` could fail typecheck, and the implementer has nothing in the spec to resolve it.

reference.md § Texts says a `parse` text refusal shows `details.message`. U27 can answer `{ reason: "parse", code: "FORMAT_NOT_JSON" }` with no `message` (the U+0000 case of U27's 'Text that is not a flow document is refused'). The spec does not say what message `textProblemRow` gives then, and no scenario covers it.

The `INVALID_RESPONSE` `ApiRequestError` that the parse helpers raise has no stated `status`, message or `requestId`. Design § Failure cases promises 'INVALID_RESPONSE text', but `flowErrorMessage` routes every other `ApiRequestError` through `errorPanelModel`, which gives `FALLBACK_MESSAGE` for an unregistered code. Which text is meant is not fixed.

The `EditorPanel` validity rules are only implied by the failing examples ("Bad Id" and "" are invalid, a 61-character title is invalid). No accepted id pattern or title length bound is stated, so the implementer has to guess where the boundaries are.

The expected recording-client entries are not shaped the same way. GET calls are `{ path, opts }` with no `body` key, and the validate call is `{ path, body: undefined, opts: undefined }`. Under `deepStrictEqual` a missing key and an `undefined` key compare differently. The recorder's exact shape per method is left to the implementer.

assumptions: U28's `loadFlow` checks the flow id against the pattern before sending, and rejects or throws `RangeError` for an id like "Bad_Name", the same way its `saveVersion` and `loadVersion` do.
U28's `loadFlow` calls the client with `{ path: "/flows/<id>", opts: { signal } }`, matching the call shape of its `loadVersion`.
In RF-1 (`rf-1-invoice-intake`), the approval node's `cases` hold approved, rejected and timeout as reference.md implies, and the archive delegate has both `next` and `on_timeout` set to `done`.
U28's editor saves first and then validates when "Validate" is pressed on unsaved text, as its own journey shows, so `GRAPH_GOOD` becomes version 2 in the browser journey.
The pytest ids `C-2619a93b` and `C-68b2dc11` are computed correctly from the formula given in tasks.md.

findings.text: design.md decision 2(d) says layers come from in-edges taken in reverse post-order of the depth-first search, and 2(e) puts unreached nodes in the layer after the last reached one. It does not say whether an edge from an unreachable node to a reachable one counts when the reachable node's layer is computed. It also does not say outright that the search follows out-edges in target-id order, though this is implied. No reference layout covers either case: in ODD, q's `next: "a"` is dropped because q's kind is unknown. An implementer could pick either reading and pass every test while drawing different layouts for such flows.

Scenario "Alice, bob and mallory read graphs from the engine" says alice creates `empty-graph` but does not name its owner team. `finance` is implied, since alice is an author only there, but it is not stated.

design.md decision 2 says `kind` is null when the field is absent or the node is not an object. It does not say what happens when `kind` is a non-string value such as a number. `kindText` handles `string | null` only, so presumably a non-string kind gives null, but this is left implicit.

Scenario "Node details are read-only text" uses a node parsed from `JSON.parse('{"kind":"end","__proto__":{"x":1}}')` but does not give the document around it: its node id, or whether there is a `start`. So the expected rows Node and Reachability are left to the implementer. Only the `__proto__` row is fixed.
